title: Terra API agent skills for building health products | Terra
summary: Give Claude, Cursor or Copilot the Terra API skills so your agent builds the integration from the current docs and gets the details right.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Terra API now ships ten agent skills and a docs MCP server, so Claude, Cursor, Copilot and any agent that reads the Agent Skills standard can build your integration from the current API instead of from what the model remembers. Install them with one command,` npx skills add tryterra/agent-skills` , or let the Terra CLI set up every agent on your machine with` terra agent setup` . The skills carry the rules that matter most across real integrations: verify webhook signatures on the raw body, acknowledge inside the timeout, dedupe chunked deliveries, and never overwrite a score with a null.


Coding agents are good at the parts of an integration they have seen thousands of times. They are much less reliable on an API with a long list of endpoints, a large number of health data sources, and a data model that appears rarely in training data. Terra API is exactly that kind of surface. The agent skills give the agent the current rules instead of leaving it to guess.


## Ten skills, with the webhook and data rules first


The[tryterra/agent-skills](https://github.com/tryterra/agent-skills) repository ships ten skills, each covering one part of the product:


Skill What it covers


[terra-unified-api](https://github.com/tryterra/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/terra-unified-api) The core API: webhooks and signature verification, data idempotency, connection lifecycle, multi-device data, testing


[terra-mobile-sdk](https://github.com/tryterra/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/terra-mobile-sdk) Apple Health, Samsung Health and Health Connect on iOS, Android, React Native and Flutter


[terra-streaming](https://github.com/tryterra/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/terra-streaming) Real-time websocket data and the Real-Time SDK on iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter and Wear OS


[terra-models](https://github.com/tryterra/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/terra-models) Running health models such as Sleep Window, Menstrual Cycle Tracker and Smart Fill over a connected user's data


[terra-vantage](https://github.com/tryterra/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/terra-vantage) Blood and DNA test kit ordering, fulfillment tracking and FHIR result delivery


[terra-planned-workouts](https://github.com/tryterra/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/terra-planned-workouts) Pushing structured interval workouts, with targets, to watches


[terra-routes](https://github.com/tryterra/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/terra-routes) Pushing GPS courses with waypoints to Garmin, COROS and Wahoo


[terra-lab-reports](https://github.com/tryterra/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/terra-lab-reports) Parsing lab report PDFs and images into standardised biomarkers, with LOINC and UCUM codes


[terra-cli](https://github.com/tryterra/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/terra-cli) Reading and changing account configuration from the terminal instead of the dashboard, and reaching any endpoint directly


[terra-mcp](https://github.com/tryterra/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/terra-mcp) Managing the account over the admin MCP server from chat assistants, with dashboard approval for sensitive changes


The one most integrations start with is[terra-unified-api](https://github.com/tryterra/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/terra-unified-api) . It carries 21 rules in five categories, ranked by impact, so an agent reads the webhook and data rules first. Four examples, each linked to the rule itself:


- [Verify the signature before parsing.](https://github.com/tryterra/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/terra-unified-api/rules/webhooks-verify-raw-body.md) Compare the` terra-signature` HMAC against the raw request body. Parsing the JSON first changes the bytes, and the check stops meaning anything.
- [Acknowledge inside the timeout.](https://github.com/tryterra/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/terra-unified-api/rules/webhooks-ack-within-timeout.md) Return a 200 within the eight-second default window and do the real work asynchronously. A slow handler gets retried, and a retry looks exactly like new data.
- [Dedupe deliveries.](https://github.com/tryterra/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/terra-unified-api/rules/webhooks-dedupe-terra-reference.md) Key on` X-Terra-Trace-Id` , because large payloads arrive in several chunks that share one reference.
- [Never overwrite a score with a null.](https://github.com/tryterra/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/terra-unified-api/rules/data-coalesce-enrichment-scores.md) Standard fields carry a superset guarantee and enrichment scores do not, so COALESCE the new value with the stored one and a user never loses a number they have already seen.


The rules are written as explicit instructions rather than descriptions, because that is what changes agent behaviour. "Only overwrite if the timestamp is newer" produces better code than a paragraph explaining why timestamps matter. Every rule comes from a pattern that shows up across real integrations, and every rule file says what to do and why.
